steps.note: The colostrum undergoes heat treatment to kill harmful bacteria like Listeria, Salmonella and E. coli; it is kept below 72 °C, where its antibodies start to break down.
The colostrum is dried; spray drying costs about 2.5 times less than freeze drying, which keeps more of the antibodies.

processing.text: A shorter heat treatment, 72 °C for 15 s, is also used, at a greater loss of IgG.

sources.text: The pasteurising times, the drying methods and what each costs the antibodies, from this review; it does not describe skimming the colostrum, so no such step is shown.
